newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot residual fuel rises, extends Thurs gain.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot residual fuel rises, extends Thurs gain.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel oil prices ended again higher Friday, extending Thursday's rise on arally in crude and natural gas prices.
Amid a quiet session, physical resid values continued were assessed higher than Thursday's levels on strength in the high sulphur materials, traders said.
Expectations of heating demand in Northeast this weekend also provided a psychological boost to the resid markets in the New York harbor and U.S. Gulf, they said.
But some participants downplayed the 20 to 30 Fahrenheit degree temperatures in the northern part of the Northeast.
"There is no significant cold weather in New York," a Northeast resid marketer said emphatically, adding overall enduser demand remained lackluster due to low natgas prices.
NYH physical one percent was assessed $20.75 a barrel, up from Thursday's $20.50 a barrel, with early October paper quote at $20.50-$20.75 versus Thursday's $20.20-$20.45.
NYH spot three percent jumped to $19.75, sharply higher than $19.25 on Thursday.
NYMEX November crude futures settled down eight cents at $24.73 a barrel and November Henry Hub natgas futures ended up 5.0 cents at $2.396 per million British thermal units.
At the Gulf, spot one percent sulphur rose to $19.88 a barrel, up from Thursday's $18.88 and three percent was valued at $19.75, up from $18.75 on Thursday.
October New York City Gate natural gas was assessed near $2.45/mmBtu, near unchanged from Thursday's quoted, compared with NYH one percent resid at $3.29/mmBtu equivalent.
